newsitem.title: USA: WASHINGTON POST FRONT PAGE - SEPT 7.
newsitem.headline: WASHINGTON POST FRONT PAGE - SEPT 7.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Sept. 7:
WASHINGTON - The remnants of Hurricane Fran caused widespread flash flooding in Virginia's Blue Ridge mountains and soaked the Washington area.
WILMINGTON, NORTH CAROLINA - Hurricane Fran caused at least 17 deaths in North Carolina and other states, prompting President Clinton to declare the state a major disaster area.
STUTTGART, GERMANY - Secretary of State Warren Christopher offered Russia a "formal charter" of cooperation with NATO.
NEW YORK - Republican vice presidential candidate Jack Kemp went to Harlem, the first campaign stop there by anyone running on a Republican ticket since George Bush went there in 1980.
WASHINGTON - States are scrambling to win a $20 million bonus for each of the five states that can show the most pronounced drop in out-of-wedlock births.
MEXICO CITY - Mexican villagers, disgusted with police corruption and inept law enforcement, have taken the law into their own hands with lynchings and beatings of suspected criminals.
